questions.question: When should you use placards?

options.text: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If the amount of hazardous materials in the truck exceeds 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of materials are being carried and warn others of possible dangers.

questions.question: When turning left with two available turning lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lane you use.

questions.explanation: Always use the rightmost lane when turning left with multiple lanes available. Large vehicles often swing right to make left turns. Using the rightmost lane lets you see other vehicles turning left and reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: When testing the trailer emergency brakes, what should you do with the trailer air supply control?

options.text: Pull it out or set it to "emergency."
Pull it out or set it to "park."
Pull it out or set it to "service."

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull it out or set it to "emergency."
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, test the trailer emergency brakes. First make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that other drivers may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, have used drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. An open window in cold weather may show a driver is impaired.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy.
When you are carrying a passenger.
When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy.
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, using a retarder can cause wheels to skid when the road is slippery. Turn off retarders when driving on wet, snowy, or icy roads.

questions.question: How long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal after you start the engine?
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, check the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a foggy area?

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a foggy area. Use low beam headlights, do not pass other vehicles, and do not stop on the road. It is best to avoid driving in fog if you can.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Create more space in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create more space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space in front of your vehicle. This makes it easier for them to pass. Speeding up is not helpful because they may tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, air loss should not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: How many red reflective warning triangles should you place when your vehicle is stopped on the road?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has red reflective triangles, place three of them as warning devices when your vehicle is stopped on the road.

questions.question: According to the National Sleep Foundation, about ____ of people have driven while sleepy.
questions.explanation: According to the National Sleep Foundation, 60 percent of Americans have driven while feeling sleepy. Another 36 percent admit to falling asleep while driving.

questions.question: A vehicle must have all of these, except:

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, warning devices (such as reflective triangles or flares), and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the flames.
Aim the fire extinguisher at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: When using a fire extinguisher, stay as far away from the flames as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the top of the flames.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens in areas where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tire tread increase the risk. Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering-equipped vehicle, you should check that:

options.text: The fluid is at the proper level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses do not contain any fluid.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the proper level.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pump, and fluid level. Look for leaks and repair them before operating the vehicle.

questions.question: If a pre-trip inspection shows the vehicle is over-length, the driver should:

options.text: Trim the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: If the load is oversize, the driver must ensure all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted and secure. The driver must also have the required permits.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Getting an adequate amount of sleep before driving
Scheduling trips during hours when you would not normally be awake
Avoiding medications that may cause drowsiness

questions.correctAnswerText: Scheduling trips during hours when you would not normally be awake
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness while driving, get a full night's sleep before your trip, have a passenger ride with you to switch drivers, schedule trips during times when you are normally awake, and avoid medications that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.explanation: When coupling a trailer, follow the correct steps in order. After connecting the air lines, the next step is to supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: Low underneath clearance causes problems when driving:
questions.explanation: Railroad-highway crossings are difficult when pulling a trailer with low underneath clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have the most trouble crossing raised crossings.

questions.question: If a tire fails, the driver should:

options.text: Keep one hand on the steering wheel and wave to other drivers with the other hand.

questions.explanation: If a tire fails, using the brakes can cause you to lose control. Avoid the brakes until your vehicle slows down. Then brake gently, move off the road, and stop.
